issue_context.title: Writing raw JSON values when using Utf8JsonWriter

review_comments: Assert after flushing the writer, that the expected json output is written when validation is off.

We should expand on the invalid json writing test cases (such as comments, trailing commas, whitespacing, partial/incomplete but valid json, etc.), and include invalid encoded data.

We also should add tests for writing valid json, but that is structurally invalid given the state of the writer.

Given the input json payload size could be quite large (more likely to be compared to a single JSON string token), it is a bit more important to try to copy in chunks rather than asking for a large contiguous buffer, similar to this issue:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ee0719079c4c4540f5adb135f002ad3ecf6c25ea/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Writer/Utf8JsonWriter.WriteValues.String.cs#L262

Might want to track that work, and follow up with user scenarios to see how important it is to copy in chunks.
Thanks, this makes sense especially as these APIs have a higher chance of being called with large payloads. I added a comment with that issue as something to investigate as a follow-up.
What should happen if the span is of length 0, i.e. empty? Same with an input string of `""`?
Oh yes, I see we throw below, because that is "invalid" json.

Add user-defined whitespace \ formatting? (here and elsewhere). That was one of the reasons for the API.

e.g.
```InlineData(true, 5, "[ 1,  1,1,1,1 ] ")]```

I think this is fine, but will pose the question nonetheless, `WriteStringValue(null)` writes the null token, should we do the same here?
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3c4d419ffe074ab62ff25a75e4127dbe7c9ee2ab/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Writer/Utf8JsonWriter.WriteValues.String.cs#L49-L52
I would say probably not, since that would violate the expectation of this only writing raw data.
